External data ingestion that enriches contacts, gated by a per-tenant admin opt-in. One ingestion pipeline
routes provider findings into **two sinks** and nothing mutates a contact without human confirmation. See
- **Enrichment provider** (`IEnrichmentProvider`, `Services/Enrichment/`) — one external data source behind a
common seam (like the email/SMS provider abstractions). Free providers always run; a provider that
`RequiresApiKey` runs only when the tenant configured a matching BYO key. Providers return findings and never
write CRM state. No concrete providers exist yet — the seam resolves to an empty set until later build steps.
- **Two sinks** — each finding routes to exactly one destination. The **structured sink** turns a
`FieldFinding` into a pending `EnrichmentSuggestion` (a proposed `Contact` field value); the **knowledge
sink** turns a `KnowledgeFinding` into an `ExternalKnowledge` row (external text stored as a citable AI
- **Signal** (`SignalFinding`, `ActivityType.EnrichmentSignal`) — an external event about the contact (e.g. a
news item from `NewsSignalProvider`, Google News RSS by company with a headline-match relevance gate). It
routes to *both* a timeline `Activity` (surfaced in the relationship stream) and a citable `ExternalKnowledge`
item (so the brief can ground on it), sharing one dedupe key so it is ingested exactly once. Informational, so
it needs no per-field confirmation. A **notable** signal (funding/liquidity/appointment keyword heuristic)
also creates a `RecommendationKind.EnrichmentSignal` Today-digest item (one open per contact per business day,
event-managed so the nightly recommendation reconciliation leaves it alone).
- **Enrichment suggestion** (`EnrichmentSuggestion`, `EnrichmentSource`) — a sourced, proposed field value
awaiting review. Mirrors the `Commitment` propose→confirm pattern: acceptance is the single write boundary to
contact state and records who confirmed it; a newer value supersedes a still-pending one.
- **External knowledge** (`ExternalKnowledge`) — a piece of external text about a contact with inline
provenance. The newest `KnowledgeEligibilityCap` items per contact stay AI-eligible; older ones are retained
for audit but excluded from retrieval, keeping the bounded token budget safe.
- **Knowledge selector** (`IExternalKnowledgeSelector`) — the RAG seam. The context builder delegates *which*
eligible knowledge items enter retrieval to this interface; the default `RecencyExternalKnowledgeSelector`
returns newest-first wholesale (no embeddings), and a future vector top-k selector can replace it without any
- **Enrichment ingestion** (`EnrichmentIngestionService`) — the two-sink router: dedupes, caps knowledge
eligibility, and owns accept/reject. **Enrichment orchestrator** (`EnrichmentService`) enforces the opt-in,
fans out over providers (fail-soft), routes findings, and writes an `EnrichmentAuditEvent` per run.
- **Enrichment opt-in** (`EnrichmentTenantSettings`, `EnrichmentSettingsService`) — off by default; a tenant
admin enables enrichment. Holds the optional BYO provider key, stored DataProtection-encrypted like Graph
mailbox tokens. Every fetch is recorded in the audit trail.

> Status: **design brief** (pre-implementation). Captured from a brainstorming/interview session on 2026-07-19.
> Records the decisions taken so far so implementation can start from a shared understanding. Not yet an ADR.
A contact record in IRE is only as rich as what a user typed or imported. Many contacts arrive from a CSV or
vCard with little more than a name and an email, so users lack the context that makes investor outreach timely
and personal — who this person is now, what firm they are at, what their company is doing, and above all *what
just changed* (a job move, a board seat, a funding round, a liquidity event). Reconstructing that means leaving
the CRM to search elsewhere, and the resulting knowledge never lands back on the record.
We want to bring external context onto the contact record for a richer relationship experience, **without**
compromising the product's privacy-preserving posture: ingesting more third-party personal data must not become
a way to silently overwrite human-entered truth, bypass consent, or create unclear provenance.
All four are the eventual target (confirmed in interview); the tension is that they differ in scope and in how
well free data sources serve them.
1. **Fill missing profile fields** — backfill company, title, city, headshot, logo, bio, social links so a
record feels complete at a glance.
2. **Signals & change monitoring** — detect and surface change over time: job/firm changes, board
appointments, the contact's company raising or having a liquidity event, notable news. The investor-relations
3. **Verify / correct existing data** — flag stale or wrong fields against an authoritative source.
4. **Feed the AI relationship layer** — make enriched context available to Relationship Briefs / Reply
Assistant, through the existing PII gateway. This is the largest goal: enrichment is not limited to data
that maps onto `Contact` fields. Any external text we can ingest about a contact (a company blurb, a bio, a
news item, a filing, a BYO-provider profile) can become **grounded AI context** — see

| Data-source strategy | **Free-first**, with an **optional BYO paid key** | Owner prefers not to pay. Free sources cover company + notable-people + news well; a tenant who wants person-level depth supplies their own aggregator key and pays the provider directly. |
| Person-level gap | Accept it on the free tier; unlock via BYO key | Free sources are weak on generic person profiles — that is exactly what paid aggregators sell. |
| First BYO provider | **People Data Labs** | Clean email→profile API, workable free tier; behind a provider seam so others can follow. |

| Privacy stance | **Conservative — sourced, suggest-then-confirm** | Nothing auto-applies. Every enrichment is stored with source + timestamp; a human confirms each change, mirroring the `Commitment` "propose → confirm → becomes CRM state" pattern. |
| Confirmation UX | **Review panel on the contact page** | Per-field accept/reject with visible provenance, localised to the record. |

| Signals surface | **Activity timeline entries + Today-digest recommendations** | Signals live in the interleaved relationship stream for context, and high-value ones (liquidity event, job change) become Today items prompting timely outreach. |

| Compliance gate | **Admin opt-in per tenant + audit trail** | Off by default; a tenant admin enables it; every fetch is audited with source + timestamp. Mirrors `AiTenantSettings.ProactiveAssistanceEnabled`. Relevant to the AU Privacy Act since we ingest third-party personal data. |

| Refresh governance | **Simple fixed schedule, no budget governor (v1)** | A nightly/weekly Hangfire job with a global throttle; skip per-tenant budget machinery for v1. (Note the risk below re: free-tier rate limits.) |
| v1 scope | **Broad v1** — fill + signals + scheduled refresh together | Owner accepts the larger build for more value sooner. |

| Enrichment sinks | **One pipeline, two sinks** | A single ingestion/provider/provenance foundation; each result routes to a `Contact`-field suggestion, an `ExternalKnowledge` retrieval source, or both. |

| Retrieval approach | **Bounded context now, RAG seam for later** | External knowledge is included wholesale (size-capped) in today's deterministic retrieval — no embeddings, no vector store. The source-builder is structured so a vector-backed top-k selector can slot in later without reworking treatments. |

| External-knowledge grounding | **Citable, no quality gate (v1)** | External docs are first-class citable sources; the AI may cite them and the user can click through to verify. No relevance/quality gate in v1 (see risk below). |
The paid aggregator (People Data Labs) is just one more provider behind the same interface; it is not required

Honest gap: individual person-level enrichment from an email is where free sources are weak; the free stack
does company + notable-people + news signals well, generic-person profiles less so.
## Two sinks: structured fields and AI-context knowledge
Enrichment is one ingestion pipeline with **two destinations**, chosen per result:
1. **Structured sink** — a value that maps to a `Contact` field (title, company, city, logo). Routes to an
`EnrichmentSuggestion` and is applied only on human confirmation (below).
2. **Knowledge sink** — external text with no clean field mapping (a company summary, a bio, a news item, a
filing excerpt, a BYO-provider profile). Routes to an **`ExternalKnowledge`** record that becomes a
first-class **retrieval source** for the AI layer.
### Why the knowledge sink is cheap here
The AI treatments do not use embeddings/RAG today. Retrieval is deterministic: for one contact, gather every
eligible row as an `AiRetrievalSource(Kind, Id, OccurredAt, Label, Text)`; the `PiiGateway` tokenises the list,
and `AiClaimValidator` forces every model claim to cite a source `Id` or be suppressed. Source kinds are a
Adding external knowledge is therefore **a new `AiSourceKind` (`ExternalKnowledge`)**, not a new subsystem.
Once an ingested document is an `AiRetrievalSource` it inherits PII tokenisation, `AiSourceAuthorizationService`
re-checks, dedup/freshness, and — the valuable part — **citations**: the AI can state "their firm raised a
Series B" and link the external source row the user clicks to verify. That is better-grounded than stamping a
### Bounded now, RAG seam for later
A single contact's enrichment is naturally small, so v1 includes external knowledge **wholesale** (with a
per-contact size/recency cap) in the existing pipeline — no vector store, no embeddings deployment. The
retrieval-source builder is factored so a vector-backed top-k selector (Azure AI Search / SQL Server 2025
vectors / pgvector + an embeddings deployment) can replace the "include all eligible knowledge" step later,
once per-contact corpora grow large enough to exceed the token budget. Treatments do not change when that swap
External documents introduce **new third-party entities** (other people named in a news article) that the
gateway was not built to tokenise — it tokenises the *contact's* identifiers. Feeding external text through the
gateway is safe for the model, but the "grounded/citable" contract now spans outside-the-CRM text. v1 accepts
external sources as citable without a quality gate; the identified risk is that noisy or low-quality material
can become citable "fact" (see Risks). A relevance/quality gate remains an easy future addition at the
Follow the `Commitment`/`CommitmentSource` shape — a proposal entity that carries provenance and becomes CRM
state only on explicit human confirmation.
- **`EnrichmentSuggestion`** (`ITenantOwned`, contact-scoped): target field (or a structured "signal"), proposed
value, current value snapshot, source, confidence, `FetchedAt`, lifecycle (`Pending` / `Accepted` /
`Rejected` / `Superseded`), and the accepting user + timestamp. Field suggestions never mutate `Contact`
directly; acceptance performs the write and records who confirmed it.
- **`EnrichmentSource`** — normalized citation (provider, URL, fetched-at), analogous to `CommitmentSource`,
so a suggestion or signal can cite where it came from.
source URL, `FetchedAt`/`OccurredAt`, and eligibility flags. Adds a new `AiSourceKind.ExternalKnowledge`
value (append-only enum) so these rows surface as `AiRetrievalSource`s. Cites via `EnrichmentSource` like any
other enrichment result. A per-contact size/recency cap keeps the bounded-retrieval token budget safe.
- **Signals** are enrichment results that are events rather than field edits. On arrival they write an
`Activity` timeline entry (new activity kind) and, when high-value, a `Recommendation` (Today item). They are
